one_liner: Pure C99 HTML5 parser using a thread-pool tokenizer/tree-builder; beats Gumbo and html5ever on parse throughput.
what_it_does: MyHTML parses a byte string or stream into a spec-conformant HTML5 DOM tree, with high-level and low-level C APIs for walking, mutating, and serializing nodes. Setup is two-step: create+init a myhtml_t (thread count, queue size, parse mode) and a separate myhtml_tree_t bound to it, then call myhtml_parse. It also supports fragment parsing, chunked/streaming input, and character-encoding detection across 39 encodings, but has no CSS selector engine.
how_it_is_fast: myhtml_init takes a thread_count and internally fans tokenization and tree construction out across a worker thread pool (thread_queue) backed by custom pool allocators (mcobject/mcsimple/mchar_async) instead of per-node malloc/free, so parsing one page overlaps tokenizing and tree-building work across cores. A single-threaded path (MyHTML_OPTIONS_PARSE_MODE_SINGLE, or building with MyCORE_BUILD_WITHOUT_THREADS=YES) exists for when thread overhead isn't worth it or POSIX threads aren't available.
when_to_use: Bulk/offline HTML5 parsing where you can dedicate a thread pool per parser instance (e.g. batch crawling, corpus processing) and want the threaded mode's throughput
C or C99 codebases that want a dependency-free, spec-conformant HTML5 tokenizer/tree builder without pulling in Rust or a GC runtime
Existing consumers via the Perl, Crystal, Elixir/Erlang, or Swift bindings who need a fast HTML5 parse step without CSS selectors
POSIX or Windows targets (source ports exist for both) where you don't need a selector engine and can build the library or vendor the source
when_not_to_use: New projects: the project's own README tells users to use the lexbor project instead, which is the maintained successor
Anything needing CSS selectors or a renderer — MyHTML only builds the tree; you'd need Modest/lexbor on top
Latency-sensitive single-page parsing on a resource-constrained host — thread-pool setup/teardown per page adds overhead unless you use Single Mode

Code that touches token/attribute text from a different thread than the parser's workers without calling myhtml_token_node_wait_for_done first, since after-token-done callbacks fire on worker threads in the default threaded mode
Projects wanting active upstream support: last commit 2025-01-15 and status is stale

integration.dependencies: none (pure C99; POSIX threads optional and can be disabled at build time)
integration.min_toolchain: C99; GNU Make (or CMake) build; POSIX threads unless built with MyCORE_BUILD_WITHOUT_THREADS=YES
integration.platforms: POSIX (Linux/macOS/BSD) and Windows source ports (source/myport/posix, source/myport/windows_nt); benchmarked on macOS/x86-64
integration.thread_safety: Not a general guarantee — per api.h doc comments, in threaded mode (default) after-token-done and tree-node callbacks fire on worker threads, not the caller's thread, and callers must call myhtml_token_node_wait_for_done before reading attributes/text from another thread; single-threaded (MyHTML_OPTIONS_PARSE_MODE_SINGLE or no-threads build) runs all callbacks on the main thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — different API shape (separate myhtml_t/tree create+init steps, high/low-level C API, no CSS selectors) vs Gumbo's or html5ever's own APIs, so it is not a drop-in swap

gotchas: In default threaded mode, token/tree callbacks run on worker threads; reading node text/attributes from the caller thread without waiting (myhtml_token_node_wait_for_done) races with the parser
No CSS selector engine — pair with Modest or lexbor if you need selectors or rendering
The upstream README itself redirects new users to lexbor, the maintained successor already in this catalog
Build flags used for the Gumbo/html5ever comparison binaries in the benchmark are not documented, so the exact magnitude of the speedup depends on how optimized those baselines were
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Prefer lexbor (its own successor, already catalogued) for any new work — same author says so. MyHTML is only worth reaching for if you're maintaining an existing MyHTML integration or need one of its non-Rust/non-C bindings (Perl, Crystal, Elixir/Erlang, Swift) and don't need CSS selectors.
verified_claims_summary: On the author's own 2016-era benchmark (466 Alexa Top-500 homepages parsed sequentially in one process, 'ex vivo'), threaded MyHTML totaled 0.509s vs Gumbo 6.130s (~12x) and html5ever 4.505s (~8.9x) on an Intel Core i7-3615QM / 8GB DDR3 Mac built with Apple LLVM 7.0.2 (clang-700.1.81); the harness Makefile default is only -O2 and library-specific build flags for myhtml, gumbo, and html5ever are unstated. MyHTML's Single Mode (single-threaded, the fairer comparison against the single-threaded baselines) totaled 0.722s, about 8.5x over Gumbo and 6.2x over html5ever.
status_note: Stale: last commit 2025-01-15, and the project's own README now directs users to the lexbor project instead; still LGPL-2.1 and small/dependency-free enough to vendor if you're stuck maintaining an existing integration.
